sections.h2: Union County Recorder's Office in Marysville
sections.html:
You will find the Union County Recorder at 233 West Sixth Street in Marysville, Ohio 43040, inside the County Office Building. The counter is staffed Monday through Friday from 7:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Call 937-645-3032 to reach the front desk. This is the official land records office for county real estate.

Every filing is indexed, which lets a searcher follow the chain of title and spot any debt still tied to the land. Images and indexes are online from 1995 forward. Older indexes now run through 1994: grantor and grantee deeds back to 1875, mortgages back to 1944, and miscellaneous records back to 1960. When an older paper has not been digitized, staff will send a copy by email, fax or mail.

The auditor and treasurer work in the same building. A deed, a tax question and a filing can often be finished in a single visit.

Recording got $5 more expensive on January 1, 2025, when Senate Bill 94 let counties add a document preservation surcharge under Ohio Revised Code 317.32. One rate covers deeds, mortgages, affidavits, easements, leases, land contracts and powers of attorney: $39 for the opening pages, then $8 for each page after.

The page chart prints $39 for one or two pages, $47 for three, $63 for five and $103 for ten. Plats and condominium drawings run $0.10 per square inch, on sheets sized 18 by 24 inches. Zoning resolutions are $50 and zoning amendments $20.

sections.h2: How a deed reaches the recorder
sections.html:
Mail a conveyance only after the Auditor has stamped it, because the Recorder will not file one without that stamp. Plan on two stops in this order: Auditor, then Recorder.

  • A representative of the buyer turns in the value statement that section 319.202 requires, on the state's DTE 100 form. An exempt transfer uses the exemption statement, DTE 100EX.
  • The conveyance fee, $4 per $1,000 of value, is paid at the Auditor's office.
  • After the stamp goes on, the Recorder files the deed.

The Auditor, Engineer and Recorder adopted a shared set of Real Estate Conveyance Standards on May 1, 2014, after public hearings in February and March of that year. Each of the three offices holds a deed to those standards, so ask your attorney or title company to compare the draft with them. Separately, section 322.02 lets a county adopt a transfer tax, so confirm with the Auditor what applies.

The office turns away any paper that displays a Social Security number unless an affidavit comes with it (section 317.082). Read through your draft for one before you submit it.

Section 317.114 sets a formatting standard, and a paper that falls short gets labeled non-conforming and billed an extra $20. Here is what the Union County schedule spells out:

  • Type of at least 10 point.
  • A blank band of three inches across the top of page one.
  • Margins of 1 inch at both sides and the bottom of every page.
  • One and a half inches of clear space above the text from page two on.

Ask your closing agent to measure the draft before it goes out. The extra charge lands on every filing that misses one of these points.

In part. Since July 15, 2024 the office has accepted eRecorded filings that are not conveyances. For a deed, call the office to ask how it should be submitted.

Residents can also sign up for a free fraud alert service. It is a notification service meant to help combat real estate fraud, and the Recorder page links to the sign-up details.

sections.h2: What to bring to the Recorder
sections.html:
Pack these items so the counter clerk at 233 West Sixth Street has no reason to send you back.

  • The original signed deed, already stamped by the Auditor if it conveys land.
  • A check or other payment for the recording fee, which depends on page count.
  • A draft that has been scanned for Social Security numbers.
  • The marginal references, if the paper releases or assigns an earlier recorded mortgage.

Clerks will describe how the records are arranged, but a full title search belongs to an attorney or title company. If your paper is unusual, phone 937-645-3032 first.

sections.h2: Liens and releases in the records
sections.html:
Read the schedule's lien entries if your title search turns up a surprise, since they show what each kind of lien costs to file and to clear. Federal tax liens and federal court judgment abstracts cost $5 to file, and a release of either costs $3. Several state liens are filed with no fee, including workers' compensation liens, Ohio EPA liens, franchise tax liens, personal property tax liens and unemployment compensation liens. A release, partial release or discharge of a franchise tax, personal property tax, tangible or intangible tax, or unemployment compensation lien costs $4.

Fixture-type UCC filings tied to land run $12, plus $4 per indexed name. Marginal references, the $4 charge that links a release or assignment to the original recorded mortgage, are billed on top of the normal recording fee. If you paid off a mortgage, check that the lender actually filed the release, because an unreleased mortgage keeps appearing in the title search.

sections.h2: From signed deed to recorded deed
sections.html:
Most Union County sales follow one route, and knowing it ahead of time can spare you a second trip.

  1. Your attorney or title company prepares the deed and compares it with the layout rules and the shared Conveyance Standards.
  2. Someone for the buyer fills out DTE 100, or DTE 100EX when no fee is owed.
  3. At the Auditor's desk you pay $4 per $1,000 of value and receive the stamp.
  4. Upstairs or down the hall, the Recorder accepts the stamped deed along with any mortgage release.

With a cash purchase there is often no new loan to record, yet the stamp and the filing charge are still required. Have the title company confirm that your old mortgage release made it into the index, since a missing release can stall a closing. Because both offices share one building, a missed signature or a page that needs fixing can be handled before you leave.

Growth is the story in Union County. The estimated 2025 population is 73,446, up 17.0 percent from the 2020 base, and 968 building permits were issued in 2025. The typical owned home is valued at $344,900, and 79.2 percent of homes are owner-occupied.

If your home is in a platted subdivision, have the title company pull the plat and recorded restrictions together with the deed. Part of Dublin and part of Plain City lie inside the county, so confirm which jurisdiction your parcel falls in when you fill out forms.

faqs.q: What is the fee to record a deed in Union County, Ohio?
faqs.a: Two pages of deed cost $39, and each page past two adds $8. Every marginal reference is another $4, and a deed that fails the formatting standard adds $20. The Auditor's conveyance fee is a separate payment.

faqs.q: Does the Union County Recorder accept deeds by mail?
faqs.a: Only when the Auditor's conveyance stamp is already on the deed. Take it to the Auditor first, then mail the stamped original with the right payment.

faqs.q: What are the Union County Recorder's office hours?
faqs.a: Walk-ins are welcome Monday to Friday between 7:30 a.m. and 4:00 p.m., at 233 West Sixth Street in Marysville. Call 937-645-3032 with questions.

faqs.q: Can I eRecord a deed in Union County?
faqs.a: The recorder has accepted eRecorded non-conveyance filings since July 15, 2024. For a deed, ask the office how to submit, since the Auditor's conveyance stamp has to be on it first.

faqs.q: What does the Union County Auditor charge to transfer a deed?
faqs.a: The conveyance fee is $4 for each thousand dollars of value. Ask the Auditor's office about any per-parcel charge and any local transfer tax.
